title: Candied lemon peel
subtitle: Blanched lemon strips simmered in sugar syrup and dried to a chewy, jewelled sweet
excerpt: Candied lemon peel is lemon rind cut into strips, blanched three times to remove bitterness, then slow-simmered in a heavy sugar syrup until translucent. The peel is dried on a rack and dusted in granulated sugar. It keeps for months and works in cakes, biscuits, or as a sweet alongside coffee.
sourceNotes: Candied citrus peel is documented in British preserving tradition from at least the 17th century. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136, documents candied orange peel. The technique for removing bitterness by blanching is standard across the tradition.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale up the peel and syrup proportionally. Use a wide pan to keep the strips in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight jar for 2 months at room temperature. Longer in the fridge.

glossaryTerms.definition: Boiling the lemon peel briefly in plain water, then draining and repeating. The process leaches out the bitter compounds from the white pith. Three blanches gives peel that is pleasantly sweet-sharp rather than bitter.

remove most of the bitterness from the pith; slow simmering in sugar syrup draws out the remaining moisture and replaces it with sugar. Dried on a rack and rolled in granulated sugar, the strips keep in a jar for months.

items.prepNote: 300 g for syrup, 100 g for finishing

content.text: Quarter the lemons from top to bottom. Peel the rind off in panels, keeping the white pith attached. Cut into strips about 5 mm wide.

Place the strips in a saucepan of cold water, bring to the boil, and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse. Repeat this process three times, starting with fresh cold water each time. After three blanches, taste a strip, it should be pleasantly bitter, not harsh.

Dissolve 300 g caster sugar in 300 ml water over medium heat. Add the blanched peel. Simmer gently for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the peel is translucent and the syrup has thickened. The peel should look jewelled, not opaque. Remove the strips with a slotted spoon and arrange on a cooling rack over a tray.

Leave the peel on the rack for 3 to 4 hours or overnight until the surface is no longer sticky and has dried to a slight crust. Toss in 100 g caster sugar to coat. Store in an airtight jar. The remaining syrup is a valuable by-product: it makes a sharp lemon cordial diluted with still or sparkling water.
